Let’s dive into Chapter 9: Expanding Influence—Speaking Beyond the Podium. As you get more comfortable and skilled with public speaking, you’ll notice that your ability to influence others starts reaching far beyond just formal presentations. These speaking skills are incredibly valuable in so many different places—whether you’re leading a team meeting, running a workshop, standing up for a cause you care about, or guiding someone as a mentor.
Expanding your influence really comes down to understanding how your communication shapes relationships and outcomes, no matter the setting. Whether you’re facing a packed audience or just talking with one person, the key principles stay the same: clarity, empathy, authenticity, and the ability to adapt.
So, how can you broaden the impact of your public speaking skills? Here are a few ways to think about:
First, there’s mentoring others. By sharing your own experiences and helping people find their voice, you help create a culture where everyone’s encouraged to grow.
Then, there’s advocating for change. When you use your communication skills to champion causes or new ideas, you can inspire people to take action together.
Another powerful approach is facilitating dialogue. By creating spaces where people feel safe to share and collaborate, you help build stronger teams and communities.
And don’t forget about the digital world. Leveraging digital platforms—like virtual meetings, webinars, or recorded videos—lets you connect with and influence people well beyond the walls of any one room.
Think about it this way: a community organizer could use storytelling and a clear message to rally support for a neighborhood project. Or a manager might open up honest conversations to solve team conflicts. In both cases, it’s your ability to communicate effectively that sparks positive change.
So, as you continue to grow these skills, remember—they’re not just for the stage. They’re tools you can use every day, wherever you want to make a difference.
